label: <DEL> step of long sequences that start with a/b/p/o/k/j/u/3/v/m
explanation: Fires almost only on the delimiter step: 98% of activation mass is at <DEL>, and 13% of all <DEL> steps are active. The rate climbs steeply with sequence length: it is near zero for L<=5, about 25% of <DEL> steps at L=8 and about 38% at L=9, and L>=8 holds about 85% of the mass. Within that, whether it fires and how strongly depends on the first one or two original tokens (the first tokens to be copied). Sequences that start with a, p, o, k, b, j, u, 3, v or m show 2-5x lift. This looks like a distributed preference over tokens, not a clean rule, so precision stays moderate. It almost never fires during the original phase (about 0.5% of mass, at late positions of L=9) or the copy phase (about 1%, on the first copy step). It does not depend on in_tok identity apart from <DEL>, or on how many digits the sequence contains. The top activations are all L=8-9 <DEL> steps.
